While the physical fold is present, the 'structured typography' is visually simulated but semantically void. I agree with marking it PRESENT for geometry (shape/layout) but note that the semantic content fails. The Router correctly marked all functional text-based checkpoints as FALSE due to gibberish. The Router was not too lenient; in fact, it was appropriately strict on the functional components.
artifact_review: The Router identified 'text_gibberish' as severity 5, which is correct and critical. The 'blur' (severity 2) and 'texture_anomaly' (severity 3) are also valid. The Perceptual Quality Auditor downplayed the issues, citing only 'slight compression,' which is a significant underestimation of the text deformation. The Image Text Auditor confirmed the gibberish with low confidence scores (<0.7) for most blocks, supporting the Router's severity 5 assessment. The Topology Auditor found a clean mask, suggesting the *object* boundary is intact, even if the *content* is flawed. No new artifacts were found by experts, but the experts confirmed the catastrophic nature of the text failure.
alignment_reasoning: The image fails the core definition of a 'menu' because it lacks readable text. While the Fine Grained Classifier identifies it as a 'menu' based on visual structure (layout, paper texture), the Functional Checkpoints (items, prices, categories) all fail. A menu without legible text is merely a prop or a hallucination of a menu. 4/9 checkpoints passed (mostly geometric/material), but the 5 failed checkpoints represent the essential function of the object. The alignment score is penalized heavily for this semantic failure despite visual resemblance.
artifact_reasoning: The primary artifact is 'text_gibberish' (Severity 5). The text is nonsensical pseudo-English ('Sunanuh', 'mpbuhe'), confirmed by the Image Text Auditor's low confidence scores. This is a structural failure of the generative model to render coherent typography. Secondary artifacts include slight edge blur and texture inconsistencies in the characters (melting letters), which contribute to the unreadability. The Perceptual Auditor's low severity rating is ignored in favor of the specific Text Auditor and Router findings.
